personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: A real OpenAPI document generated from the validators means I can type a client against it instead of guessing.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: A bearer key and a curl is something I can plug into our PHP tools today, no gimmick in the way.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: Our tools can start a bug fix themselves, and I can see every PRD of the workspace in one call.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: One workspace-wide key that starts agent work on any repository: who started the 3am pull request?

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: A customer tool could file a bug and get a fix PR without me learning the harness.

objection.text: One workspace-wide string that can start agent work on any repository is a lot of power. When a job opens a PR at 3am, I need to see which key started it, not just which owner made the key.

rounds.fit: fits persona:F-E Developer ✓ · persona:B-E DEv ✓ · persona:Paul - Product Manager ✓ · persona:Irisa ✓ · persona:Lead Engineer ✗ until the key is named on each job and limited by repository

personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: A test fails when a v1 route is missing from the reference, so the doc cannot drift.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: One error shape, a keyset cursor that never repeats a row, and 401s I can rely on.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: Listing and starting bug fixes ships now; creating a PRD waits for the next one.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: Every job names its key and its maker, a key can be held to one repository, and it dies when its maker leaves.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: The bug fixes list has no state yet, so a customer-facing tool still has to look at GitHub.

rounds.fit: fits persona:F-E Developer ✓ · persona:B-E DEv ✓ · persona:Paul - Product Manager ✓ · persona:Lead Engineer ✓ · persona:Irisa ✓ with the missing bug state named in Decisions
